Class NitriteSortPlan

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.data.nitrite.runtime.read.NitriteSortPlan
@Internal public final class NitriteSortPlan extends Object
How the ORDER BY of one read is carried out.

Nitrite orders by a stored field only, and places nulls first before reversing the whole comparison for a descending key - so a find expresses ascending/nulls-first and descending/nulls-last, and nothing else. A sort that stays inside that goes to the find, where an index can serve it. A sort that does not - one ordering by a computed expression, or asking for nulls at the end Nitrite does not put them - is carried out here instead, over the documents the find returns. Skip and limit then have to come off the find as well, because they would otherwise cut the result before it is ordered.

Since:
5.2.0

      public void withholdWindow(org.dizitart.no2.collection.FindOptions options)
      Takes the row window off the find, for a sort the find cannot carry: the window would otherwise cut the result before apply(List, Collator) orders it. The caller leaves the ordering off the find by not calling applyNativeOrder(FindOptions).

      options - the find options, left without a window
